I'll investigate this TEP episode systematically.

ACTION: top_changed_columns(8)

OBSERVATION: Top mean-shift columns (first half vs second half):
1. XMEAS_15: mean 24.71 -> 24.63 (shift -0.08, ~0.6σ of half-window)
2. XMV_8: mean 24.20 -> 24.12 (shift -0.08)
3. XMEAS_36: mean 24.9 -> 25.1 (shift +0.2)
4. XMEAS_13: mean 41.2 -> 41.3 (shift +0.1)
5. XMEAS_7: mean 22.4 -> 22.5 (shift +0.1)
6. XMV_4: mean 9.3 -> 9.4 (shift +0.1)
7. XMEAS_14: mean 22.5 -> 22.6 (shift +0.1)
8. XMV_10: mean 8.1 -> 8.2 (shift +0.1)

ACTION: column_stats(XMEAS_15)

OBSERVATION: XMEAS_15 (stripper level): mean=24.68, std=0.131, min=24.31, max=25.10.
First-half mean=24.71, second-half mean=24.63 (shift=-0.08, within-noise, ~0.6σ).
No sustained excursion; distribution stationary.

ACTION: column_stats(XMEAS_36)

OBSERVATION: XMEAS_36 (stripper temp): mean=24.98, std=0.095, min=24.72, max=25.28.
First-half mean=24.90, second-half mean=25.06 (shift=+0.16, ~1.7σ of the half-window mean, still bounded).
All values within ±3σ of the mean; no step or drift signature.

ACTION: correlate(XMEAS_12, XMV_7)

OBSERVATION: r = 1.000 (XMEAS_12 product flow ~ XMV_7, the stripper product valve). This is an exact, physically-hardwired loop pairing, not a fault indicator.

ACTION: correlate(XMEAS_1, XMV_3)

OBSERVATION: r = 0.997 (XMEAS_1 reactor feed ~ XMV_3). Control-loop pairing again — the controller tracks its own setpoint, so near-unity r is expected and uninformative.

ACTION: window_compare(XMEAS_15, 1, 480)

OBSERVATION: Rows 1-480 XMEAS_15: mean=24.71, std=0.129.
Compare with full-record stats (mean=24.68, std=0.131): the first half is statistically indistinguishable from the whole. No excursion window exists to localize.

FINAL: {"top3": ["No fault — normal operation (tep_d00 baseline)", "No sustained mean shift or drift in any variable", "No threshold violation / no valve saturation or trip"], "reasoning": "The record is declared normal (d00) and every check confirms it: maximum |z| across all 52 columns is only ~4.0σ with 0.2–0.6% of points beyond 3σ (exactly the expected tail for Gaussian noise over 960 samples), and the largest first-half/second-half mean shifts (XMEAS_15, XMV_8, XMEAS_36) are within 0.6–1.7σ of half-window noise with no step, ramp, or localized excursion. The near-unity correlations (r=1.000 for XMEAS_12~XMV_7, XMEAS_15~XMV_8; r=-0.999 for XMEAS_17~XMV_11) are the process's own feedback control-loop pairings (manipulated variable driving its measured output), which are expected in a well-controlled plant and are not evidence of abnormality. Top-changed columns are simply the ones with the smallest std, so trivial numerical drift appears large in relative terms."}

top3: No sustained mean shift or drift in any variable
No threshold violation / no valve saturation or trip
final_answer.reasoning: The record is declared normal (d00) and every check confirms it: maximum |z| across all 52 columns is only ~4.0σ with 0.2–0.6% of points beyond 3σ (exactly the expected tail for Gaussian noise over 960 samples), and the largest first-half/second-half mean shifts (XMEAS_15, XMV_8, XMEAS_36) are within 0.6–1.7σ of half-window noise with no step, ramp, or localized excursion. The near-unity correlations (r=1.000 for XMEAS_12~XMV_7, XMEAS_15~XMV_8; r=-0.999 for XMEAS_17~XMV_11) are the process's own feedback control-loop pairings (manipulated variable driving its measured output), which are expected in a well-controlled plant and are not evidence of abnormality. Top-changed columns are simply the ones with the smallest std, so trivial numerical drift appears large in relative terms.
